text:
alex: incident-bot fired: KV cache eviction-rate spike in us-west-2, streaming tail latency p99 > 3s, clients reporting stalls. seeing lots of small-object evictions. tagging oncall.
incident-bot: ALERT: kv_eviction_rate increased from 12/s to 320/s in last 5m on shard gw-12; p95 decode latency 420ms -> 780ms, p99 decode latency 1.2s -> 3.6s. impact: streaming responses stalled, ~6% request errors.
maria: looking at dashboards now — prefill queue depth is very high, but decode workers are idle-ish. prefill:get_rate ~ 450/s, decode:process_rate ~ 120/s. feels like prefill vs decode imbalance.
sachin: confirmed slab fragmentation on gw-12. free chunks are < 4KB so we get a lot of evictions for longer KV entries. eviction log shows lots of small pages being reclaimed then reallocated.
taylor: any customer impact observed? which tenants?
maria: Customer impact: increased tail for streaming endpoints for a handful of high-rate tenants in us-west-2 (customers: acme-inc, fastchat). Error rate uptick correlated with streaming stalls. Not a broad outage but SLOs breached for those routes: streaming.p99 > 2.5s (SLO 1s).
sachin: grabbing redispatch/metrics and recent allocation snapshots. pushing a quick histogram:
```
kv_alloc_chunk_size: median 8KB, but free-run: 2KB
kv_evictions_by_reason: fragmentation=68%, ttl_expire=22%, size_pressure=10%
prefill_vs_decode: prefill_rate: 450/s, decode_rate: 120/s, prefill_queue_len: 340
streaming_tail_p99: 3.6s
```
alex: Okay. Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle prefill for non-critical tenants 2) temporarily increase slab allocation to reduce fragmentation 3) route some traffic to spare capacity in eu-west-1 4) ramp up decode workers (if safe). Thoughts?
maria: Throttling prefill easiest and lowest-risk. We should reduce prefill concurrency for acme-inc and fastchat first.
sachin: increasing slab size requires a rolling config change across gw nodes — takes ~10-15m and risk of transient alloc churn. prefer prefill throttles + scale decode workers.
taylor: can we do a partial slab bump only on gw-12? There are per-shard configs.
sachin: yes but still a restart of the allocator on gw-12 needed. safer to do throttles now.
ops-bot: RUNBOOK NOTE: when eviction_rate > 200/s and fragmentation > 50% => consider prefill backpressure or isolate hot tenants.
alex: Action plan (live):
- maria: apply prefill concurrency limit to acme-inc + fastchat, reduce target rate to 50% (now)
- sachin: spin up +20 decode workers on gw-12, but keep autoscaler paused (3m)
- taylor: prepare slab config bump for gw-12 as fallback (ready in 10m)
- alex: open support ping to acme-inc/fastchat and advise degraded streaming for next 30m
maria: applying prefill throttle now: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/prefill/throttle -d '{"tenants":["acme-inc","fastchat"], "ratio":0.5}'`
incident-bot: CONFIG CHANGE applied: prefill throttle ratio=0.5 for acme-inc,fastchat on us-west-2 (applied by maria).
maria: observed prefill_rate drop to ~220/s, prefill_queue_len -> 120, decode_rate still 140/s (workers scaling up). p95 decode 430ms, p99 decode 1.1s. streaming.p99 -> 1.6s.
sachin: decode workers +20 active. memory pressure modest. eviction_rate down to 80/s. fragmentation still high but stabilizing.
taylor: prepping slab bump: config patch ready `allocator.slab_size_map[gw-12] = 65536` (current 32768). will stage if we see >200/s again.
ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT NOTE: slab config requires allocator process restart on gw-12; expected brief latency spike on restart.
alex: agree hold off on slab restart unless metrics regress. Maria—monitor for next 20m, notify if p99 > 2s or eviction_rate > 150/s.
maria: will monitor; setting alert annotation.
(10m later)
maria: metrics holding: streaming.p99 1.05s, errors back to baseline ~0.7%. eviction_rate 45/s. prefill/decode closer to parity (prefill 210/s, decode 200/s).
taylor: customer notifications sent?
alex: yes I posted to accounts:#acme-inc and #fastchat with status and mitigation steps.
incident-bot: NOTE: SLO breach window now closed for most tenants. recorded p99 breach start_ts=1791122334 end_ts=1791122900 for streaming.us-west-2 for tenants [acme-inc, fastchat].
sachin: I'm going to keep slab bump patch in staging for 30m; if fragmentation doesn't drop below 40% we'll schedule the allocator restart.
maria: leaving throttles in place for extra 10m to ensure queue drains.
alex: handing off to oncall-next for follow-up. Handoff summary:
- root cause: KV slab fragmentation on gw-12 causing small-chunk churn + prefill/decode imbalance; manifested as eviction wave -> tail latency + streaming stalls for a few tenants.
- mitigations performed: prefill throttles applied to impacted tenants, +20 decode workers added, alerting/notifications sent.
- current state: streaming.p99 ~1.05s, eviction_rate ~45/s, fragmentation ~52% (slowly declining), prefill/decode ~= parity.
- recommended follow-ups for next oncall: consider allocator slab bump on gw-12 during low traffic window, run heap/alloc traces for longest-lived entries, enable targeted cache warming for impacted tenants to avoid cold churn, and review prefill worker autoscaling thresholds.
alex: @oncall-next you're up — will link dashboards and recent allocation dump in the thread.
oncall-next: ack, will take it from here. I'll watch for re-regression and coordinate slab restart if needed.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): impact reduced, monitoring continues. Incident severity: Sev-2 -> monitoring.
alex: thanks everyone, great fast coordination.
maria: noted post-incident: add a prefill backpressure automatic toggle in optimizer to detect imbalance and auto-throttle before eviction accelerates.
sachin: +1; adding a ticket: INF-8246: auto-detect prefill/decode drift and apply adaptive throttles.
taylor: I'll schedule slab defrag runbook review.
(End of thread)
